_comment: Carry to R9-RO-9 (#1922) from R9-RO-5. The round-9 roster is not on main, so this file is the in-tree destination.
While this and the roster brief disagree, the newer is right.

carries.control: Run, at your merge base, a listing of git ls-files spelled through canon (counts.mjs canonList) and the same listing unspelled, and test the globs tools/audit/briefs/** and dev/governance/roles/** against each. On the R9-RO-5 head the old glob matched the canon spelling and none of the real paths, and the new glob matched the real paths and none of the canon spelling. The null is the other column: a glob that matches the real tree and not the canon list is what rule-binding reports as matching no tracked file, because that check reads the canon list. Re-run the same two columns. When they agree, this constraint is spent.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust the column result above. Re-run it at your merge base before editing a rule paths glob. policy-docs restores policy_lint.mjs and brief_lint.mjs from the base, and rule-binding walks the canon spelling.
carries.brief: R9-RO-9 drops the old-path lookup. In that same change, and not before, move each rule's paths globs off the canon spelling (tools/audit/briefs, docs/HANDOVER.md, docs/delivery, docs/plan) onto the paths the files have after R9-RO-5. A glob written only at the new path, while canon still spells listings the old way, is reported by rule-binding as matching no tracked file, on the restored grader as well as on the branch. Leaving the globs on the old spelling after canon is removed is the other failure: they then match nothing. The two edits are one edit.

carries.control: At your merge base, check origin/main's tools/policy out over the branch (git checkout origin/main -- tools/policy) and run node tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs and python3 -I tools/policy/agreement_py.py --run. R9-RO-8 first rewrote the audit-find.js and audit-verify.js prompt paths and moved D11's governance_cost.py and d11lib.py; against that head the base check-wave-script printed 165 passed, 5 failed (the arms matching the old spelling of dev/audit/config/*.json) and the base agreement_py.py raised FileNotFoundError on tools/audit/round4/D11/governance_cost.py. R9-RO-8 reverted both, so the base graders pass against its head; the null is that earlier head.
carries.remeasure: Re-run the two commands at your merge base. When no base copy still names the old paths, this constraint is spent.
carries.brief: R9-RO-9 moves tools/audit/round4/D11/governance_cost.py and d11lib.py under dev/audit/rounds/round4/D11/ (they stay at the old path through R9-RO-8 because the base agreement_py.py imports them there; drop the two INERT_EXCEPT entries, the entities.py path and the two closures.json entries in the same change) and rewrites the audit-find.js and audit-verify.js prompt and path text (seatDir, JUDGE, sweep, ISSUES, ledger, schema, scopes) together with check-wave-script.mjs's matching strings, only after main carries the updated graders. It also rewrites the leftovers listed under Figures of the R9-RO-8 body: the pre-move pathspecs and `if test -f` guards in governance.yml, tests.yml, pr-contract.yml and prepr.sh, the locate-wrapped old names, the corpus_excluded.json and cfr_exclusions.json keys, policy prose and ADR citations, CODEOWNERS line 49. A grader a job restores from the base reads the old name until the base carries the rewrite, so drop a guard only after the base has the new name.
